prompt: Suricata runs as an IDS on one machine and as an IPS on another. What makes the difference?
hint: The section says it is often the same program.

choices.text: Where it sits and what it is allowed to do
choices.why: Right. Beside the traffic, or inline with the power to drop.

choices.text: The IPS reads a newer rule language with more keywords
choices.why: The rule on ips is the sensor's with one word changed.

choices.text: The IPS decrypts the traffic the IDS skips
choices.why: Encryption is not what separates them.

choices.text: A larger rule set
choices.why: Both ran the same single rule.

prompt: Match each situation to what it costs or means.
hint: The table in the section.

pairs.left: a false positive in an IDS
pairs.right: an alert somebody reads and dismisses

pairs.left: a false positive in an IPS

right_distractors: the rule is deleted by the sensor

prompt: A new rule fires on a hundred harmless requests a day. Where does it belong for now?
hint: Which system can afford to be noisy?

choices.text: In detection, until its false positives are known to be rare
choices.why: Right. Promoted to blocking only after it has been watched.

choices.text: Inline at once, because blocking is safer than alerting
choices.why: Inline it would block those hundred customers.

choices.text: Deleted, since a rule with false positives is useless
choices.why: Rules are born noisy and tuned in detection.

choices.text: Inline, with its alerts switched off
choices.why: It would still refuse legitimate requests, silently.

prompt: After inline.sh rewires the lab, where does the machine ips sit?
hint: Nothing from outside reaches the shop without crossing it.

choices.text: On a mirror port of the DMZ switch
choices.why: That is a sensor's place, on a copy.

choices.text: On the cable between fw and the DMZ
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: Inside fw, as a second set of firewall rules
choices.why: It is a separate machine with two interfaces.

choices.text: Between the DMZ switch and www
choices.why: It sits in front of the switch, not behind it.

prompt: With only the sensor watching, remote asked for /admin/. What did remote get?
hint: Does an IDS stand in the way?

choices.text: The admin console
choices.why: Right. An IDS writes it down and lets it pass.

choices.text: A timeout, because the sensor dropped the request
choices.why: The sensor has no address and drops nothing.

choices.text: A 403 page written by the sensor
choices.why: The status in the alert was 200.

choices.text: A reset the sensor sent to both ends
choices.why: The curl printed the console's answer.

prompt: The sensor's rule matches when the requested path ___ with /admin.
hint: The keyword after content in the rule.

prompt: In fast.log, what does [1:1000101:1] identify?
hint: Compare it with sid and rev in the rule.

choices.text: Priority, rule, packet count
choices.why: The priority is printed separately.

choices.text: Which rule fired, and its revision
choices.why: Right. sid 1000101, rev 1.

choices.text: The connection number, its port and its priority
choices.why: The connection is at the end of the line.

choices.text: The sensor, the alert count and the priority
choices.why: 1000101 is the sid in the rule.

prompt: Which priority did fast.log give the admin-path alert?
hint: classtype decides it.

prompt: Which field of the alert in eve.json turns it into a finding?
hint: Whether it worked.

choices.text: http.status: 200
choices.why: Right. The admin console was served to the internet.

choices.text: alert.signature_id: 1000101
choices.why: That says which rule, not what happened.
That says who asked.

choices.text: dest_port: 80
choices.why: That says to what, not whether it worked.

prompt: The same alert, but http.status is 404. What does that suggest?
hint: The section reads 404, 403 and 200 in turn.

choices.text: The admin console was served to the internet
choices.why: That is what 200 means.

choices.text: A guessed path that does not exist
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: A control refused the request
choices.why: That is a 403.

choices.text: The IDS blocked the request
choices.why: The IDS blocks nothing; action is allowed.

prompt: Why does the sensor's alert say action allowed?
hint: What does an IDS do on a match?

choices.text: The rule was written with the action allow
choices.why: The rule's action was alert.

choices.text: An IDS lets each match pass and records it
choices.why: Right. It is the honest word for detection.

choices.text: The requester's address was on an allow list
choices.why: There is no allow list in the rule.

choices.text: The proxy had approved the request first
choices.why: The IDS does not ask the proxy.

prompt: Which rule message serves the analyst reading it at 3 a.m.?
hint: It says what happened and why it matters.

choices.text: rule 7 match
choices.why: It names the rule and says nothing else.

choices.text: admin path requested from outside
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: sid 1000101 fired
choices.why: The sid is in the alert already.

choices.text: HTTP policy-violation event
choices.why: That is the category, not what happened.

prompt: ips is cabled in and nothing runs on it yet. What happens to the shop?
hint: What forwards the packets?

choices.text: It is unreachable
choices.why: Right. A machine that forwards nothing is a cut cable.

choices.text: It works unchecked, since ips is a plain bridge
choices.why: Suricata is what joins the two sides.

choices.text: It works, and ips logs each request
choices.why: curl timed out with exit 28.

choices.text: The admin path is refused and the rest passes
choices.why: No rule is loaded yet.

prompt: What changed in the rule on ips, compared with the sensor's?
hint: Read the start and the end of the rule.

choices.text: The sid, so both rules can coexist
choices.why: The sid is 1000101 in both.

choices.text: drop instead of alert, rev 2
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The path became /admin/ with a slash
choices.why: That is the fix in the last section.

choices.text: flow:to_server was removed
choices.why: The flow keyword is unchanged.

prompt: What exit status did curl report for the admin request that ips dropped?
hint: curl -m3 gave up.

prompt: Order what a request from remote crosses on its way to www, with ips inline.
hint: ips sits on fw's DMZ cable.
items: fw sends it out on its DMZ cable
ips reads it on one interface and decides
ips writes it out of its other interface
the DMZ switch delivers it to www
trap: ips sits between fw and the switch, not after the switch.

prompt: eve.json on ips shows the admin request as blocked. What did www receive of it?
hint: Suricata saw the path in the first packet of the request.

choices.text: A request it answered with 403
choices.why: The 403 would come from a control on the server's side.

choices.text: Nothing: the request never reached it
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The full request, since blocking stops only the answer
choices.why: The request itself was dropped.

choices.text: A reset sent by ips
choices.why: curl waited and timed out; nothing was reset.

prompt: Why was /admin-guide.html blocked?
hint: Read the path next to the rule.

choices.text: It starts with /admin, which is all the rule checks
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: The help page is served from the admin console
choices.why: It is a page for customers.

choices.text: Suricata kept blocking remote after its first drop
choices.why: The rule matches paths, not addresses.

choices.text: The request came from the same address as before
choices.why: The address is not what the rule tests.

prompt: Which are sound responses to the admin-guide false positive? Choose all that apply.
hint: The fix, and the general lesson.

choices.text: Narrow the content to /admin/ with the slash
choices.why: Right. The help page no longer matches.

choices.text: Watch a rule against real traffic before it goes inline
choices.why: Right. That is how you learn what else it matches.

choices.text: Raise the rule's priority
choices.why: Priority orders alerts; it does not change what matches.

choices.text: Change alert.action to allowed in eve.json
choices.why: That field records what happened; editing the log fixes nothing.

prompt: Suricata on ips was stopped and the shop became unreachable. What is that behaviour called?
hint: What passes when nothing inspects?

choices.text: Failing closed
choices.why: Right. Nothing passes unless it was inspected.

choices.text: Failing open, with traffic unchecked
choices.why: The shop stopped answering.

choices.text: A bypass joining the two ports
choices.why: A bypass would have kept the shop up.

choices.text: The rule dropping traffic after it stopped
choices.why: No program was left to apply a rule.

prompt: An IPS appliance goes in front of the shop, where availability comes first. What should be tested before it goes live?
hint: Stop it on purpose and watch the link.

choices.text: That its bypass passes traffic when its software is stopped on purpose
choices.why: Right. The front door should fail open, and that is tested.

choices.text: That it fails closed when its power is cut
choices.why: Closed suits a payment segment, not the front door.

choices.text: That its rules each fire once in the lab
choices.why: That tests the rules, not what the link does when it stops.

choices.text: That it adds no latency to the traffic
choices.why: Inline, each packet waits for it.

prompt: An IPS guards a payment segment, and uninspected payment traffic is worse than none. How should it fail?
hint: The table's last row.

choices.text: Open, with a bypass
choices.why: That lets payment traffic through uninspected.

choices.text: Closed, accepting an outage
choices.why: Right.

choices.text: As an IDS on a mirror port instead
choices.why: An IDS stops nothing, failing or not.

choices.text: Open, with an alert when it stops
choices.why: Traffic still flows uninspected during the gap.

prompt: An IDS alert shows /backup.zip requested from outside, action allowed, status 200. Where does the investigation turn?
hint: Read the last two fields the way the lesson read /admin/.

choices.text: To why the server handed the file out
choices.why: Right. A 200 moves the question to the server.

choices.text: To the requester's address, to block it and close the case
choices.why: The file already left; the gap is on the server.

choices.text: To the IDS, which should have stopped it
choices.why: Allowed is what an IDS does on every match.

choices.text: To nothing, since allowed means policy permitted it
choices.why: allowed describes the IDS, not the policy.
